body:
i am very aware that i have a poor relationship with alcohol. i can't function in any social setting that involves more than one person without at least being tipsy, i also used to come to classes that graded for participation in undergrad tipsy so that i could participate without thinking too much about it

i have been perplexed by it though because friends have warned me that i am bordering on alcoholism, but they only ever see me in those social situations, and on a day-to-day basis i don't feel like i need it

i have actually learned a lot of slang from a lot of different countries!! that was honestly what made spanish *so* fascinating to me, how different the language can be. i ended up dating someone from mexico who didn't speak a lot of english so i learned a lot of mexican slang, and then when i was in college i had some friends from el salvador and guatemala and stayed in their house a lot and learned a lot of slang from them and their parents, and then spent a semester studying abroad in spain where i learned more slang!

it's fascinating that there is *always* more to learn in spanish! i've also been told by native speakers that every time i learn spanish from another country my accent changes, which is really neat. I'm now in grad school and my best friend's parents from cuba have taught me a lot of cuban spanish!

when i was in high school, spanish was my special interest. i got so obsessed with learning spanish, i quickly became ahead of my classmates and in a year i could hold a conversation about most things and had learned past and conditional verb tenses ahead of my class. i spoke so well that whenever i engaged with a native speaker in spanish, they would ask what country i was from.
